rule: Name the bounded thing a person wants, bind it to existing stock and an existing Store evaluator, and do not create new machine authority.

jobs.plainIntent: Cut one 2x4 square to the finished length I enter.
jobs.currentAppPinNote: The established Board path is pinned separately. Later Store candidates descend from that Stage-2 Store state; this reconciliation does not move the application pin.
refuseOrStop: missing or unsupported finished-length input remains unresolved
finished length outside the published application slice is not clamped
Store may refuse, leave unresolved, or report unavailable from its own basis

jobs.plainIntent: Route a rectangular blank in 3/4 in sheet stock and leave it attached with reference tabs for later separation.
jobs.currentAppPinNote: The current System published-job path asks this existing Store evaluator at its exact published-job pin. This reconciliation does not move that pin.
refuseOrStop: blank below the declared minimum or larger than the parent sheet is refused
missing tabs or route-depth basis stops or refuses as declared by the envelope
machine-local language such as G-code is refused
generic curvilinear demand is not silently interpreted as this rectangle

jobs.publicName: Centered arched cutout in 1/2 in ply
jobs.plainIntent: Route the published centered arched opening in a full 48 x 96 in 1/2 in sheet reference, using opening width and rise to define the circular segment.
jobs.currentAppPinNote: The current System published-job path is pinned to the canonical centered S-001 runtime. This reconciliation keeps the full 48 x 96 parent and centered 48 x 36 work field; it does not broaden edge-routing capability.
refuseOrStop: missing chord or rise remains unresolved
a supplied radius that contradicts chord plus rise is refused
the whole routed profile must remain inside the centered 48 x 36 work field
requested exterior rating remains unresolved for the published 1/2 in sheathing SKU
machine-local language such as G-code is refused
notClaimed: edge routing outside the centered work field
